items.description:
Escalates Green Tier’s Healthy Defaults and Tiered Access to Screens
by Grade Band, includes: whitelist-only access in
grades K–8, a maintained blocklist in grades 9–12, cameras off by
default, non-instructional platforms (including social media and
gaming) blocked outright, AI tools disabled by default district-wide,
personal data fully wiped before device reassignment, and EdTech
audit, reduction and transparency.
items.title: Black Tier 1: Next steps on healthy defaults on school devices

items.description: Sets the standards every digital product, including AI, should be measured against before it reaches a classroom, including safety, privacy, educational effectiveness, equity, and independence from the industry it’s meant to evaluate. Most districts already have a review process in place, and are hesitant to give authority to an outside body. That said, there are many reasons why parents deserve a seat at the table, and why this process needs to be continuously updated and transparent.
items.title: Black Tier 3: Digital Product Standards

items.description: This priority moves social media out of the school’s official communication toolkit entirely, which means no staff-to-student contact on Instagram or TikTok, no team group chats on Snapchat, no student photos posted to a public school account without real parental consent. It also takes a closer look at the way social media is accessed and used at school by students by blocking social media access on school-issued devices, and preventing social media use for learning.
items.title: Blue Tier 1: Social Media Use Policy Playbook

items.description:
This priority sets a grade-band framework for school-issued devices
including hands-on, print-based instruction in the earliest grades,
shared cart-based devices in middle school, and one-to-one devices
only in high school with real caregiver opt-in and safeguards. It pairs
naturally with Healthy Defaults and the Social Media Use Policy, but
it doesn’t require either one: a district can adopt this on its own.
items.title: Blue Tier 2: Tiered access to screens by grade band playbook

items.description:
A Tech Advisory Committee is a standing parent and community
voice researching and recommending how the district approaches
technology. It gives families a real, standing voice in the district’s
technology direction.
items.title: Blue Tier 3: Tech Advisory Committee Playbook

items.description:
Blue tier priorities ask a bit more of a district than
Green: they touch handbooks, device management, and vendor review. They can be adopted locally, on a district's own timeline.
items.title: Blue Tier: Pick up the pace playbooks: Social Media Use Policy · Tiered Access to Screens by Grade Band · Tech AdvisoryCommittee (TAC)

items.description:
Black tier priorities are the most technical asks in
this system as they touch IT infrastructure,
procurement, and (for Pause on High-Risk AI and
Digital Product Standards) may require School
Committee action rather than administrative
implementation alone. They’re a natural next step
for districts that have already moved on Healthy
Defaults or stood up a Tech Advisory Committee,
but none of the three is a prerequisite for another.
items.title: Full Black: Next Steps on Defaults and Digital Product Standards Playbooks

items.description:
This is the easiest, lowest-cost place to start. There's no policy to pass
and no IT ticket to file. All you need to do is have a conversation with
a teacher about what happens during “free time” in the classroom.
items.title: Green Tier 1: Ditch "Free" Screen-time

items.description:
A bell-to-bell, phone-free school day is the most legislatively
advanced of all our priorities. Massachusetts’ House and Senate have
already agreed on the personal-device provisions of pending
legislation, which, contrary to what many districts claim, means
districts do not need to wait for a final vote or a policy from DESE to
act.
items.title: Green Tier 2: Phone-free Schools Policy

items.description:
This priority asks districts to work with IT to enable a set of settings
most schools already have access to. These include downtime hours,
after-hours restrictions, and blocked full YouTube access, allowing
only teacher-embedded videos.
items.title: Green Tier 3: Healthy Defaults on School Devices

items.description: Three easy asks you can work on today in your district. Ditch Free Screen time, phone free schools, and healthy defaults on school issued devices.

items.description:
Kids finding workarounds isn’t a reason to abandon defaults, filtering, or device restrictions — it’s part of why layered guardrails matter in the first place. Use this guide to feel informed,
so the district doesn’t have to explain the basics before you can get to the actual ask. You don’t need to understand the technology deeply
— you just need to know what to ask, and what a good answer sounds like.
